A quartz crystal oscillator operates based on the piezoelectric effect, where the crystal can vibrate at two closely spaced resonant frequencies: one series and one parallel.  
The series resonance occurs when the crystal's inductive and capacitive reactances cancel in the series branch, and the parallel resonance occurs when the crystal's motional inductance resonates with the parallel (shunt) capacitance.  
Both frequencies are utilized in oscillator circuits depending on the circuit configuration and load capacitance.
